name: Felix feUSD
oneLiner: feUSD is Felix Protocol's Liquity-v2-fork dollar on Hyperliquid, minted from overcollateralized CDPs against HYPE, kHYPE, wstHYPE, and bridged BTC.
collateral: HYPE, kHYPE, wstHYPE, and UBTC (feUBTC) via overcollateralized CDPs on Hyperliquid (Liquity V2 fork); the live adapter reports four active branches
pegMechanism: Overcollateralized CDP (Liquity V2 fork) with direct redemption for $1 of collateral; interest-rate-sorted redemption queue (lower-rate positions redeemed first); stability pools absorb liquidations

oracleRisk.summary: Felix feUSD uses separate external-oracle PriceFeed contracts for four isolated Liquity V2-style branches, with freshness checks, shutdown on feed failure, Stability Pool offsets, and branch-local debt redistribution.

branchApplicability.rationale: Felix documents WHYPE, kHYPE, UBTC, and wstHYPE as independent collateral branches with separate PriceFeed, TroveManager, Stability Pool, and risk-parameter contracts. Each branch therefore requires its own oracle and liquidation evidence row.

branches.label: WHYPE collateral branch
branches.summary: The WHYPE branch uses its dedicated Felix PriceFeed contract to value collateral for Trove health and liquidation.

feeds.provider: Felix branch PriceFeed with external AggregatorV3 source
feeds.path: External HYPE/USD answer -> WHYPE PriceFeed -> Trove ICR

branches.fallbackBehavior: The PriceFeed rejects reverted, zero, or stale oracle answers and triggers branch shutdown; after shutdown it retains the lastGoodPrice for urgent redemption pricing rather than switching to a live secondary market feed.

collateralParameters.note: The branch has independently deployed MCR, CCR, SCR, liquidation-penalty, and mint-cap parameters; Troves become liquidatable immediately below the branch MCR.

branches.liquidationMechanism: Any caller may liquidate a Trove once ICR is below MCR. Branch Stability Pool feUSD first offsets and burns debt for seized WHYPE; any uncovered debt and collateral are redistributed across active Troves in the same branch.
branches.backstop: The branch-local Stability Pool is the first-loss liquidation backstop; just-in-time feUSD or branch-local redistribution to active Troves handles debt not covered by Stability Pool deposits.
branches.shutdownOrBadDebtBehavior: Oracle failure or TCR below SCR can shut the branch, freeze borrower operations, and enable fee-free urgent redemptions at a collateral bonus using lastGoodPrice. Felix documents that uncleared debt may remain after shutdown and that a separate bad-debt solution is not implemented.

branches.label: kHYPE collateral branch
branches.summary: The kHYPE branch uses its dedicated Felix PriceFeed contract to value the liquid-staking collateral for Trove health and liquidation.

feeds.provider: Felix branch PriceFeed with external AggregatorV3 source
feeds.path: External collateral price answer and branch conversion -> kHYPE PriceFeed -> Trove ICR

branches.fallbackBehavior: The PriceFeed rejects reverted, zero, or stale inputs and shuts down the branch. If only the kHYPE/HYPE market feed fails while HYPE/USD and the canonical staking rate remain live, it switches to HYPE/USD multiplied by that canonical rate; failure of HYPE/USD, USDC/USD, or the canonical rate instead falls back to lastGoodPrice.

bridgeRouteRisk.summary: FEUSD has HyperEVM/Hyperliquid deployments and candidate evidence points to Hyperliquid canonical routing. With no separate issuer bridge protocol resolved, the route is reviewed as canonical ecosystem bridge exposure. 2026-07-20 cohort dc-1 pass: HyperEVM row confirmed native feUSD; HyperCore row remains unresolved (non-EVM).

blacklistabilityReview.evidence: Explicit Yes retained: reviewed metadata or audit notes identify direct seizure, freeze, blacklist, privileged burn, proxy-upgrade, or chain-governance intervention authority despite decentralized governance labeling.

mintAuthority.summary: feUSD is minted from Liquity-v2-fork CDPs on Hyperliquid (HyperEVM) against HYPE, kHYPE, wstHYPE, and bridged BTC at user-set interest rates. Each of the four active branches authorizes its BorrowerOperations and ActivePool contracts to mint feUSD, for eight current token-level minters. The feUSD token (0x02c6a2fa) is an EIP-1967 proxy whose ProxyAdmin (0x44a600c0) is owned by a central admin proxy (0xf42fdd95). That admin proxy's own ProxyAdmin (0xdf1293b4) is owned by a Gnosis Safe 1.3.0 multisig (0x699090e7, 3-of-6, no modules, no guard). The same multisig is the ultimate upgrade authority for the entire Felix protocol.

upgradeability.controlRef: Felix admin multisig (ultimate upgrade and parameter authority)

controls.label: Felix WHYPE BorrowerOperations
controls.capDescription: User debt issuance is constrained by WHYPE collateral requirements and the branch maxDebtCap; the Felix admin can raise that cap.
controls.evidence: At HyperEVM block 37553335: feUSD token (0x02c6a2fa58cc01a18b8d9e00ea48d65e4df26c70) is an EIP-1967 proxy (implementation slot = 0x444322c3c54908fa5a7842a4f3ff085ec67f2598, proxy admin slot = 0x44a600c031dbdf652500f4a6d84b168056f13692). ProxyAdmin confirmed by getProxyImplementation returning the implementation address. At block 40636026, CollateralRegistry reported exactly four active collaterals; the WHYPE registry resolved this BorrowerOperations address and feUSD borrowerOperationsAddresses(address) returned true.

controls.label: Felix WHYPE ActivePool
controls.capDescription: Mints only accounted WHYPE-branch aggregate interest and batch-management fees derived from branch debt; it has no independent arbitrary-mint entry point.
controls.evidence: At block 40636026, the WHYPE registry resolved this ActivePool address and feUSD activePoolAddresses(address) returned true. The current ActivePool source mints only accounted aggregate interest, Stability Pool yield, and batch-management fees.

controls.label: Felix admin multisig (ultimate upgrade and parameter authority)
controls.evidence: Latest HyperEVM getOwners() on Safe 0x699090e73c4077ef2af42773b31788c6564f079c returned 6 owners, threshold 3, no modules, no guard. This refresh replaces the prior stale owner snapshot that also contained a malformed 39-hex address.

review.evidence: On-chain reads traced the full Felix admin chain: feUSD token (0x02c6a2fa) → ProxyAdmin (0x44a600c0, owner=0xf42fdd95) → nested admin proxy 0xf42fdd95 (implementation 0xd2fe30df..., ProxyAdmin 0xdf1293b4) → 0xdf1293b4 owner()=0x699090e7 → Gnosis Safe 1.3.0 (3-of-6, 6 current EOA signers, no modules, no guard, fallback handler=0x017062a1). Rechecked at HyperEVM block 40435040; the proxy, implementation, and ownership chain is unchanged. The same 0xf42f proxy owns the Felix AddressesRegistry (0x9de1e57049c475736289cb006212f3e1dce4711b). The 3-of-6 Safe is the ultimate admin authority. At block 40636026, CollateralRegistry totalCollaterals() returned 4 and indices 0-3 resolved WHYPE, UBTC, kHYPE, and wstHYPE while index 4 reverted. Each branch registry resolved one BorrowerOperations and one ActivePool address, and all eight corresponding feUSD authorization mappings returned true.
